parts.ask: Prove, using algebra, that \((n + 1)^3 - n^3\) is odd for all \(n \in \mathbb{N}\).
parts.method: Proof by exhaustion: \(n\) even, then \(n\) odd

steps.text: \(n\) even: let \(n = 2k\), where \(k\) is an integer.

steps.why: Two times an integer, plus 1: odd.
Keep the bracket: the minus applies to every term.

parts.answerText: In both cases \((n + 1)^3 - n^3\) is one more than an even number, so it is odd for all \(n \in \mathbb{N}\).

check.answers: proof by exhaustion: the assert re-expands both cases and tests n up to 200
